exclusions.description: Open sacroiliac joint fusion is not covered for any other indication, including the specified conditions

conditions.value: located at or close to the posterior superior iliac spine (PSIS) with possible radiation into buttocks, posterior thigh, or groin and can point to the location of pain (Fortin Finger Test)

conditions.notes: provocative examination maneuvers that stress the sacroiliac joint (e.g., FABER test, thigh thrust, pelvic gapping test, pelvic compression, Gaenslen's test)
ADLs defined as feeding, bathing, dressing, grooming, meal preparation, household chores, and occupational tasks

value: Anti-inflammatory medication (one or more of: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (oral or topical) unless contraindicated, Acetaminophen)
A trial of Physical Therapy in the last 12 months (supervised, attendance >75% of sessions, minimum of 3 visits) unless conservative therapy is not appropriate and documented why

conditions.value: At least 2 intraarticular SI joint steroid injections (location confirmed by contrast spread or both A/P and lateral views). If patient fails to get 80% or greater pain relief, second injection at least one month later.

If steroid injections unsuccessful, trial of at least 2 anesthetic injections in the lateral branch (location confirmed by contrast spread or both A/P and lateral views), with at least 80% reduction in pain, 2 week minimum between injections.

If anesthetic injection is successful, patient should have an RFA ablation (not covered/required for Medicare). If anesthetic injection not successful, or if post ablation pain is not reduced by less than 80% after 1 month, consult with SI joint surgeon.

conditions.notes: e.g., hip osteoarthritis, L5-S1 spine degeneration, tumor, infection, fracture
